learn.hook: Who cooks, who fixes the fan, who reads you bedtime stories? In a family, everyone has a part to play!
points: A family is the first group we belong to. It cares for us, protects us and teaches us values.
In a joint family, grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts and cousins live together. In a nuclear family, parents and their children live together.
Each member has roles and duties: earning, cooking, cleaning, shopping, caring for babies and elders, and helping with studies. Children help too, for example by tidying their things.
Sharing work fairly among everyone, whether boy, girl, man or woman, makes a family happy and strong.
Elders pass on stories, recipes, skills and traditions to younger members, and children often help elders with phones and new things.

example.q: Ananya's mother works in an office, and her father cooks dinner on weekdays. Her grandmother helps her with homework. What does this show?
steps: Different members are doing different jobs.
The jobs are shared based on time and skill, not on fixed ideas about who 'should' do them.
Everyone helps, so the family runs smoothly.
example.answer: Family members share roles and help each other.

learn.reallife: When you lay the plates for dinner or water the plants at home, you are doing your role in the family.

learn.hook: When a wedding happens in a village, neighbours lend chairs, cook together and decorate. That's community!
points: A community is a larger group of people who live near each other or share something in common, like a village, a neighbourhood or a housing society.
Communities help each other during festivals, weddings, illness and disasters like floods.
Important community values include cooperation, sharing, respect for others, honesty and caring for common spaces like parks, wells and ponds.
Communities also look after shared resources, such as cleaning a village pond or planting trees together.
An ancient Sanskrit saying, 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam', means 'the world is one family', extending these values to everyone.

example.q: After heavy rains flood some homes in a village, what might the community do?
steps: Neighbours give shelter to families whose homes are flooded.
People share food, clothes and help clean up.
Together they recover faster than any family could alone.
example.answer: They cooperate and share, helping everyone recover.

learn.reallife: Resident welfare associations in cities, langars and community kitchens, and village clean-up drives are all communities in action.

games.title: Values in action
pairs: working together to clean the pond
lending chairs for a neighbour's wedding
planting trees in the park together

items.text: A group of people living in the same area or sharing something in common is a ___.
'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' means the world is one ___.
Working together for a shared goal is called ___.
Parks and village ponds are ___ spaces.

options: Only the members of one house
A group of people who live near each other or share something in common
quiz.explain: Villages, neighbourhoods and housing societies are examples of communities.
steps: A community is a larger group of people.
They live near each other or share something in common.
Examples: a village, a neighbourhood, a housing society.
Answer: A group of people who live near each other or share something in common
quiz.mistake: Thinks a community is only one's own family

quiz.explain: This Sanskrit saying means the whole world is one family.
steps: 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' is an ancient Sanskrit saying.
It means 'the world is one family'.
Answer: The world is one family
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with other well-known sayings

quiz.q: Which is an example of cooperation?
options: Each person throwing waste into the pond
Neighbours cleaning the village pond together
quiz.explain: Cooperation means working together for a shared goal.
steps: Cooperation means working together for a shared goal.
Neighbours cleaning the pond together do that.
Answer: Neighbours cleaning the village pond together
quiz.mistake: Confuses cooperation with competition or neglect

quiz.q: Why is it important to care for common spaces like parks?
options: They belong to nobody, so it doesn't matter
Everyone uses them, so everyone should keep them clean
quiz.explain: Common spaces serve all of us, so all of us share the duty to protect them.
steps: Parks, wells and ponds are common spaces.
Everyone uses them, so everyone must care for them.
Answer: Everyone uses them, so everyone should keep them clean
quiz.mistake: Thinks shared spaces are nobody's responsibility

quiz.q: How do communities usually help during floods?
options: By staying away from each other
By sharing shelter, food and help with cleaning up
quiz.explain: In difficult times, communities support those in need.
steps: Communities help each other during disasters like floods.
They share shelter, food and help with cleaning up.
Answer: By sharing shelter, food and help with cleaning up

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a community value?
quiz.explain: Wasting shared water harms everyone; the others are values that help communities.
steps: Community values: cooperation, sharing, respect, honesty, caring for common spaces.
Wasting shared water harms everyone.
So 'wasting shared water' is NOT a value.
Answer: Wasting shared water
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise a harmful habit

quiz.q: A housing society collects money to repair its water tank. What value does this show?
quiz.explain: Members share the cost and the benefit of a common resource.
steps: The water tank is a shared resource.
Members share its repair cost.
This shows sharing responsibility for common resources.
Answer: Sharing responsibility for common resources
quiz.mistake: Does not see the shared benefit

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of a community?
quiz.explain: A community is a group of people, like the residents of a village.
steps: A community is a group of people.
The people of a village are such a group.
A tree or a bicycle is not. Answer: The people of a village

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Why do neighbours help each other? Isn't it enough to care for my own family?'
teach.praise: Now I know! Communities cooperate and share, and the saying 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' reminds us the world is one family!
teach.nudge: How does a community help its members? And what does 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' mean?

revise.summary: A community is a larger group of people who live near each other or share something in common. Communities cooperate, share, respect others and care for common spaces and resources.
